question: Does a fixed confidence-dependent transition cost improve official external possession spell F1 over exact cost-3 Viterbi on the adopted dense ensemble, while preserving short possessions and feed-like performance?
hypothesis: Reducing the cost only for probability-supported directed transitions can recover genuine brief possessions while retaining cost-3 smoothing where an edge lacks support.

candidate.name: dense_boundary_confidence_v1
candidate.formula: For a directed state change i->j at adjacent rows t-1,t, penalty = 3 * fps/10 * (1 - sqrt(p[t-1,i] * p[t,j])); same-state penalty is zero.

control: Exact replay of experiments.supervised.decode(probabilities, model_periods, fps, switch_cost=3).
prediction_source: Frozen current dense ensemble native H/A/D probabilities, averaged before decoding; no refitting or probability alteration.

cohort.protocol: Existing full-provider external holdout, whole match/provider exclusions respected by upstream models.
cohort.scoring: Official evaluation/possession_metrics.py via experiments.metrics.evaluate_tracking; paired within each match and view.

guardrails.primary: Aggregate clean spell F1 must improve; summarize paired per-match deltas.
guardrails.feed_like: Aggregate mean across the two feed_like views must not decline.
guardrails.short_spell: Report recall for GT alive spells shorter than 3 seconds; candidate must not reduce this aggregate.
integrity: break decoding at period and timestamp discontinuities
same probabilities and rows for both arms

provenance_note: No dense frame-level fragmentation-versus-merging audit was available at freeze time; this study tests the stated decoder mechanism without choosing a direction or threshold from holdout labels.
